terms.definition: A technique where a language model writes out intermediate reasoning steps before giving its final answer. It tends to improve performance on multi-step problems.
Further training of a pre-trained model on curated input-output examples, so it learns to imitate the desired responses.
A way of training in which a model generates outputs, receives a reward score for them, and is adjusted to make higher-reward outputs more likely.
The pre-trained base language model from DeepSeek, before instruction tuning, on which R1-Zero and R1 are trained.
The paper's first model, trained with RL directly on the base model without any supervised fine-tuning stage.
The paper's final model, trained through a multi-stage pipeline combining supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
To train a smaller model on the outputs of a larger, stronger model so it inherits some of its abilities.
A reinforcement learning algorithm that samples a group of outputs per question and scores each relative to the group, avoiding a separate learned value model.
In RL, the model's rule for choosing outputs; here, the language model itself being optimized.
A measure of how much better an output's reward is than a baseline expectation. In GRPO the baseline is the group's average reward.
A widely used RL algorithm for training language models that uses a clipped update and typically a learned value model.
A measure of how different one probability distribution is from another. Here it is penalized to keep the trained policy close to a reference policy.
A hyperparameter setting how far the policy's probability ratio may move before being clipped in the GRPO/PPO objective.
A separate learned model that predicts the expected future reward from a partial output. PPO uses one to estimate advantages.
A method used in PPO to estimate advantages from rewards and a value model, with a coefficient λ that trades off bias and variance.
Describes rewards computed by fixed programmatic checks, such as answer matching or running test cases, rather than by a learned model.
A reward that checks whether a response's final answer is correct, for example by matching a reference answer or passing test cases.
A reward given when the response follows the required structure, such as putting reasoning inside think tags.
When a model exploits flaws in a reward function to score highly without actually doing what the designers intended.
Learned neural networks that score responses, as opposed to fixed rules. They can be outcome-based (scoring final answers) or process-based (scoring steps).
A high-school math competition whose problems have integer answers, used here as a reasoning benchmark.
The expected probability that a single sampled response is correct, estimated by averaging correctness over several sampled responses.
A decoding method that samples many reasoning paths and takes the most common final answer (majority vote).
A small initial set of curated examples used to fine-tune a model before RL begins, giving it a readable starting style.
A reward equal to the proportion of words in the chain of thought that are in the target language, used to reduce language mixing.
Generating many candidate responses and keeping only those that pass a filter, such as having a correct final answer.
An open-ended benchmark in which an LLM judge compares model responses to instructions; prompts are generally less demanding than Arena-Hard.
A benchmark of challenging open-ended prompts drawn from Chatbot Arena, scored by an LLM judge.
A benchmark measuring whether a model follows explicit, verifiable formatting and content instructions.
A benchmark of real-world code editing tasks across multiple programming languages.
A human-validated subset of software engineering tasks where a model must resolve real GitHub issues.
A dataset of competition-style math problems graded by difficulty level; MATH-500 is a 500-problem evaluation subset.
A coding benchmark of recent algorithmic contest problems collected over time to limit contamination.
An online competitive-programming platform; the paper uses its problems and reports a rating and a percentile versus human participants.
A benchmark of graduate-level multiple-choice science questions in physics, chemistry and biology.
A harder version of the MMLU multi-subject benchmark, with questions needing deeper reasoning.
A grouping of science, technology, engineering and math subjects.
When benchmark questions or close variants appear in a model's training data, which can inflate its test scores.
A contiguous sequence of n tokens or words. Matching n-grams is a way to detect overlap between training text and test questions.
A sampling setting that controls randomness in generation; lower values make outputs more predictable, higher values more varied.
The amount of computation, such as number of generated thinking tokens, a model spends when answering a question.
Sampling several independent answers and choosing the most common one.
A search method that explores possible continuations as a tree, guided by simulations and a value estimate.
A model architecture in which only a subset of specialized sub-networks is activated for each token.
A prompt crafted to get a model to bypass its safety training and produce content it would normally refuse.
An external layer around the model that flags risky conversations by keywords and has another model review them, adding safety beyond the model's own.
A crowdsourced platform where users vote between anonymous model responses, producing human-preference rankings.
